title: Hesitation and Challenge
subtitle: You can always count on someone to be there for you, waiting to support you.

trails.title: Bygone Days
trails.description: An aged, delicate newspaper—a remnant of the distant and worn past.

content.text:
Exclusive Interview: Meet the Floor Ritual Prodigy

Charlotte O'Hagan: "Claiming My Sunshine"

    In a stunning performance at the Uluru Games' Floor Ritual event, 11-year-old Charlotte O'Hagan claimed the gold medal with her original move, the "Geranium Dance." This victory not only crowned her this year's champion but also broke a two-century-old record, making her the youngest winner in the event's documented history, with the previous record being set in 1802 by "Greenfingered Anna," who was 13 at the time.

    The O'Hagan lineage is steeped in the traditions of ritualistic Arcane Skills. Charlotte's great-grandfather, Douglas O'Hagan, who famously once entered the hidden stone gate at the Giant's Causeway, and authored the arcanist text The Gate of All Gates: Rituals of Unlocking and Summoning. Her grandmother, Elizabeth Baker O'Hagan, earned a bronze medal in the same Floor Ritual event back in 1866 ...

    ......

    Charlotte shared her thoughts and experiences in a post-competition interview (See page 4 for the full interview).

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Be careful. Now you can spit it out. Right.

items.speaker: Patient I
items.text: *puke*
Vomit plunges into a bucket. Tooth Fairy doesn't spare it a second thought.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: That's the fifth one today. I added a bit of powder into the candy to loosen up their phlegm. It should help them breathe a little easier.

items.speaker: Nurse
items.text: Thank you so much, Doctor. We really had no idea what to do with this new variant of tuberculosis. You and the Foundation have been a real asset to us.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: You're welcome. This is a matter of vital health for all of us. I'm very glad to see the treatment is proving effective.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: And I hope that our clinical experience here might contribute to solving this "fog curse" as well.

items.speaker: Nurse
items.text: All I'm hoping for is for this mess to end soon, so we can go watch the Games together.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Really, so the staff here are fans of the Uluru Games as well?

items.speaker: Nurse
items.text: Not just the staff. Everyone here loves a bit of sport! We're always listening to the broadcasts over the radio down in the ward.

items.speaker: Nurse
items.text: It's all quite motivating. Sometimes we even get the patients out onto the commons to practice.

items.speaker: Nurse
items.text: Something about the coming of a big sporting event always brings people together.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: That's all very good to hear. But actually, it was this poster that grabbed my attention.
She points to the small poster pinned beside the bed.
The picture is faded. It's too difficult to make out the face of the athlete.

items.speaker: Nurse
items.text: Ah! That's her!

items.speaker: Nurse
items.text: Gorgeous, isn't she?

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: May I ask who she is?

items.speaker: Nurse
items.text: She happens to be this patient's favorite competitor of all time.

items.speaker: Nurse
items.text: She collected all of her posters and clippings. She even keeps a few photos of her as a bookmark, and in her purse.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Her favorite ritualist ...

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: Looks like you haven't had a proper guest in ages. Have you forgotten how to make a cup of tea?

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: You like to presume, don't you?

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: So, why are you here, then? Just to enjoy the sound of a door slamming in your face?

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: Oh, how terrible of me for wanting to visit an old friend.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: So then, Ms. Bartley, you came all the way down from Yorkshire just to gawk at an old rival? I should feel lucky, should I?

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Truth is I don't care to chatter about with you, not now, not ever.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: So you can just turn around and march yourself home. Flutterpage, back to business.
After glancing at Caroline, Willow turns and gives Flutterpage a look.
But Flutterpage is too busy staring at Caroline, her face vacant.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Why'd you send her away like that? She just wants to practice with you. She likes you.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Focus on your stopwatch, on the count of three. No time to waste.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: She's still there.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: She's none of our concern.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: And you ain't seen each other in a long time. Bet she misses you a lot.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: For Pete's sake, Buzzie, no one does something like that just out of the goodness of their own heart. She has her reasons.
Flutterpage obediently closes her mouth but can't help herself from giving Caroline a reluctant glance.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: Charlotte, you know she's right.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: I have missed you. I want to see you, but if you really want to know the reason ...

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: I want to challenge you again.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: The question is, do you?

items.speaker: Nurse
items.text: Do you know her?

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Charlotte O'Hagan ...

items.speaker: Nurse
items.text: Oh. Right! That's the name.

items.speaker: Nurse
items.text: Truth is, if it weren't for our little patient, I doubt I'd remember her.

items.speaker: Nurse
items.text: Most people think she's too old to compete now—that she's retired to God knows where; others say she's become an addict, wasting her life away.

items.speaker: Nurse
items.text: I guess I heard in the gossip rags that some people think she's keeled over and died.

items.speaker: Nurse
items.text: Too bad for this young lady, but I doubt we'll ever see her in the Games again.

items.speaker: Nurse
items.text: Wherever she is, she's like as not to lose, even if she did compete.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: You just want to announce to the world you've beat me, eh? Think that'll be a fair challenge, do you?

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Perhaps you ought to find someone a little more your speed, someone who is still in one piece.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Again, Ms. Bartley.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Please turn around. I haven't any sort of tea you'd like.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: You have changed, haven't you, Charlotte?

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: Hmph!
After a brief moment of surprise, Caroline throws a ribbon at Willow.
The ribbon lashes fiercely, grazing the side of Willow's body before shooting past her.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: What the blazes are you doing?

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: What?
Caroline pulls the ribbon back toward her, the cup landing squarely in her hand. She stands there calmly, her eyes still on Willow.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: You just said you don't have any tea I'd like, but I think this one is just to my taste.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Wow, Ms. Willow, that ribbon is amazin'! It can go from long to short in a second!

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Aye, a little toss of the ribbon to take control of an object at a distance of 10 meters, catch an object after a turn. You did it. Well done. But your aesthetics were lazy.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: You're controlling the angle of your left shoulder, which is good, but it only means you're compensating for your poor stance.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: Heh. What then, are you expecting me to say thank you?

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: No need. Thank yourself for all that hard practice you must have done over all those years. You're almost good enough, now. Almost.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Keep the cup. Let's go back to our timing, Flutterpage.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Alright. Bye bye, Ms. Swan!
For a moment, Caroline stands there motionlessly, cup in hand.
Then, she gradually lowers her eyes, places the cup on the fence post, and turns to walk away.
She has barely walked a few steps when Willow's voice reaches her from behind, not loud, but clear.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Oh, by the by.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: The ribbon technique you just did. I know you learnt it from me, from my performance at the Beltane Exhibition Match. Am I right?

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: Hmm?
The tone of her voice makes it almost impossible to simply walk away.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: Excuse me?

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Each and every move, you copied it from my routine, right down to the ribbon.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: What?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Ms. Swan, your face is all red, like my daddy's face when he reads a funny joke in his Punch books.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: Me ... Learnt from you?

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: You were taunting me right in front of my face, with my own routine, the very innovator that made it.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: I suppose it was just an attempt to win my approval, was it?

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: You really think that, don't you?

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: But, I'm afraid you're not different than when we last competed, Caroline. Aye, you're diligent, but you were never graceful enough.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: That's what holds you back from glory in Floor Ritual. Your aesthetic sensibility, it's all you've ever needed, but you still don't have it, do you now?

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: You won't make any real progress reusing my old routines. Not unless you find your own way to express your pneuma and your own signature.
Shame and regret slowly creep across Caroline's face as she struggles to contain her anger.
Then, it bursts forth.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: You really are full of yourself, aren't you, Charlotte?

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: Do you know how many titles I've won at the international tournaments? The Desert Floor Ritual Open, The Aurora Cup World Championship, and many others, let alone Uluru itself!

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: The name Caroline Bartley has long surpassed yours! I am the uncontested top seed in these Games. The records of my skills, my own skills, are in the training manuals for new witches.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: Do you even know anything about the state of the competition these days? The rules and scoring systems are entirely different and higher in every way. The limits you once broke through are now considered standard for beginners.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: Hah! But indeed, I learnt it all from you.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: Face it. You've been left behind. You're no longer the model of perfection.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: You're just a shooting star that shined too briefly but eventually fell away. I am the rising sun. My name will be eternal in this sport, long after yours is forgotten.
Willow smiles, her back turned to Caroline.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: So be it.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Go on. Be the glorious sun.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: And leave this fading star alone.
Caroline stands in shock as a couple of doves take flight, leaving behind a few drifting feathers.

items.speaker: Little Lisa
items.text: Aunt Martha!

items.speaker: Nurse
items.text: Lisa, you're back! We were just talking about you.

items.speaker: Little Lisa
items.text: About me? What about me?

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: About your dream and your favorite competitor.

items.speaker: Little Lisa
items.text: Oh, oh, you mean Charlotte O'Hagan?

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Yes, we—

items.speaker: Little Lisa
items.text: That's great! But Mr. Fog needs us for a project!

items.speaker: Little Lisa
items.text: He says we can still have the Games if we all work together! Then maybe everyone will be able to attend the qualifiers! Maybe even Charlotte O'Hagan!

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: A project?

items.speaker: Nurse
items.text: What sort of project?
The girl's cries draw the attention of everyone in the hospital, creating a buzz of confusion.

items.speaker: Patient I
items.text: Give me a break. What are they planning to do this time? Another useless bill that won't pass the House of Lords?

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Sorry for interrupting. Did I hear you mention Mr. Fog?

items.speaker: Little Lisa
items.text: Yes, Mr. Fog! He said he's making something that will lift all the fog from London!

items.speaker: Little Lisa
items.text: It's his great invention!

items.speaker: Little Lisa
items.text: With everyone's help, we can build a huuuge machine, but he says we'll need lots and lots of things, such as, um, pistons for the mechanic lung, and ...
Calm, steady footsteps grow nearer, and a large hand tousles the little girl's hair.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: I'll take it over from here. Thank you, Lisa.

items.speaker: Little Lisa
items.text: Mr. Fog!

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Mr. Fog?
